_comment: Rendered by web/index.html. Edit this, not the HTML. Keep 'blocked' honest — a page that is all green is a page nobody believes.

milestones.name: Corpus measures
milestones.note: Caption coverage, anchor coverage, sibling ambiguity and page sharing, computed on two extraction pipelines that share no code and no models. Model-free, so it reproduces anywhere.

milestones.name: Placement metric
milestones.note: Ground truth derived from the source typesetting rather than annotation. Retriever and generator both removed, so what is measured is the placement mechanism alone.

milestones.name: External validation
milestones.note: All six MRAMG subsets now run, pooled into the three domains the published table uses. Academic 69.12 against 65.28 for the best published system. Lifestyle 55.00 against 62.23 — a loss, reported as one. The Web domain admits no claim at all: every candidate there is already a gold image, so precision is arithmetic rather than earned.

milestones.name: Second benchmark, and the gate on external gold
milestones.note: MMDocRAG (2055 questions, 4 domains, NeurIPS 2025) added as a second external benchmark. Two results: the cross-encoder matches BM25 where descriptions are author-written (63.38 vs 63.48) — so the MRAMG win was the representation, not the ranker — and the vision gate, run for the first time against gold we did not author, adds +13.65 precision / +7.81 F1 over the identical pipeline without it. Still behind GPT-4.1's published 80.7.

milestones.name: Admission-rule study
milestones.note: 6,819 questions, one persisted score file, the full rule grid across all seven evaluation units. The finding is not the one we expected: the boundary that matters is absolute-vs-scale-free, not where the floor sits. The frozen floor scores macro 51.45 with a worst unit of 11.31 (News: 86% mute); even 0.001 leaves News 48% silent. Every scale-free rule — plain top-K or relative-to-max — lands within ~1 macro point of every other (67.6–67.7), no unit collapsing. Family choice: 16 macro points. Choice within the family: one.

milestones.name: End-to-end generation
milestones.note: MRAMG's own generation protocol on Academic, 200 questions, same 8B SEA-LION generator in both arms. Statistical half: inline insertion beats post-hoc selection on F1 (61.71 vs 55.91) — a loss, reported as one — while ours keeps +10 precision, and the admission study's pre-registered rule replicated out-of-sample (+7.6 F1). Judged half, blind, paired, now under TWO independent vendors' judges: the generator's selection advantage replicates (relevance and effectiveness, CIs exclude zero, both judges), comprehensive is a tie twice, and on POSITION the anchor join ties under the first judge (48:49) and wins outright under the second (−0.09, CI [−0.16,−0.01], 56:36). Under neither judge does the generator place better than the join.

milestones.name: Academic margin, bounded
milestones.note: Bootstrap over questions (B=20,000): pooled IP 69.12, 95% CI [61.43, 76.56]; 15.7% of resamples fall at or below the published 65.28. The paper now says 'higher, not significantly higher' — a four-point margin on 200 questions is real but not resolvable.

milestones.name: Selection result
milestones.note: Demoted to preliminary: F1 0.605 against human annotation on 48 items carrying 19 positive links. The externally scored version of the same comparison — the MMDocRAG composed run — now carries the weight instead.

milestones.name: Annotation scale-up
milestones.note: A second annotator on the existing 48 items, and more items after that. We tested whether an automated judge could substitute and it cannot at this scale, so this is back to being the binding constraint with no shortcut available.

milestones.name: Bibliography
milestones.note: Every entry checked against its arXiv or publisher listing page. No entry remains marked unverified.

milestones.name: Authorship and venue
milestones.note: The author list is deliberately unfilled in main.tex and CITATION.cff. Venue is undecided: the running header currently reads as a preprint, and the title was rewritten to name the method rather than the deployment.

milestones.name: Second judge, cross-vendor
milestones.note: MiniMax-M3 sat the identical selection-judging exam — same protocol, same pools, same images, 360 human-labelled pairs — and failed it: kappa 0.362 at 2.76x permissiveness, against the incumbent's 0.556 at 1.24x. It was therefore NOT licensed as a gate, and the refusal is the result: kappa is a per-model credential and now demonstrably does not transfer across vendors. On the end-to-end judged metrics (a different instrument, validated by inter-judge agreement r=0.64–0.79) it strengthens every conclusion instead.

milestones.name: Judge-scaled estimation
milestones.note: Built, and it does not work at this scale. The validity gate passes now (enrichment 0.95x) and the judge agrees with a person at kappa 0.556, replicating an earlier independent measurement. But four of five confidence intervals fail to narrow and one widens 19%: with 165 judged questions against 45 annotated, the ratio is far below what prediction-powered inference needs. Human annotation remains the constraint.

notes: The method is a join over data the layout parser already produced. No model, no training, nothing tuned per corpus — so the claim is not scoped to a language or a document genre.
The Indonesian textbook corpus is the stress case, not the scope: only a fifth of its figures carry a printed caption, so a caption-matching pipeline fails there in a way caption-rich corpora hide.
